{{short description|Measure of efficacy in clinical trials}}
{{refimprove|date=June 2012}}

'''Response-rate ratio''' is a measure of efficacy of therapy in [[clinical trial]]s. It is defined as the proportion of improved patients in the
[[Treatment groups|treatment group]], divided by the proportion of improved patients in the [[Scientific control|control group]].{{citation needed|date=June 2012}} The same term has been used in [[marketing]].<ref>{{cite journal |jstor=1250681 |pages=71–73 |last1=Berdie |first1=D. R. |last2=Anderson |first2=J. F. |title=Mail Questionnaire Response Rates: Updating Outmoded Thinking |volume=40 |issue=1 |journal=The Journal of Marketing |year=1976 |doi=10.2307/1250681}}</ref>
